subject.title: Feature request: fallback model chain for compaction and LCM summaryModel

question: Should the fallback contract be split between core embedded compaction and Lossless/plugin-owned summary models, or should OpenClaw add a generic context-engine/plugin SDK fallback seam before any user-facing config is added?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix crosses core config, provider/auth routing, and an external context-engine plugin contract; automation should not choose that public API shape alone.

options.title: Approve split contract
options.body: Add a documented core `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` path for embedded compaction and require Lossless to own `summaryModel` fallback config or request a narrow SDK seam.

options.title: SDK seam first
options.body: Pause core config work until maintainers design a generic context-engine summarizer fallback contract that Lossless and future engines can implement.

options.title: Close as out of scope
options.body: Decline core fallback config and direct users to plugin/provider-level retry mechanisms, leaving the exact compaction model behavior unchanged.

recommendation.title: Approve split contract
recommendation.body: Add a documented core `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` path for embedded compaction and require Lossless to own `summaryModel` fallback config or request a narrow SDK seam.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history across compaction behavior and config/docs touchpoints and is the best available routing candidate for the product/API choice.
